tool.name: GFF3 validator
tool.description: check GFF3 files against the GFF3 1.26 specification
tool.command:
#import re ## Name the input after the dataset so that reports show a meaningful file name. #set $name = re.sub(r'[^\w\-.]', '_', str($input.element_identifier)) #if $name.strip('.') == '': #set $name = 'input.gff3' #end if ln -s '$input' '$name' &&
#set $options = '' #if $biology.run == 'yes': ## Compression is detected from the content, so the dataset is used as is. #set $options += " --genome '" + str($biology.genome) + "' --translation-table " + str($biology.translation_table) #end if #if $header == 'require': #set $options += ' --require-header' #elif $header == 'skip': #set $options += ' --no-header' #end if #set $options += ' --max-findings ' + str($max_findings)
## gff3-validate exits 0 when the file has no errors, 1 when it has errors and ## 2 when the run is incomplete (unreadable input or genome). Exit status 1 is ## a successful validation, so it is mapped to 0; any other status stops the ## job with that status. accept_invalid() { status=\$?; [ "\$status" -eq 1 ] || exit "\$status"; } && gff3-validate $options --format text -- '$name' || accept_invalid && gff3-validate $options --format html -- '$name' > '$report_html' || accept_invalid #if 'json' in $extra_reports: && gff3-validate $options --format json -- '$name' > '$report_json' || accept_invalid #end if #if 'sarif' in $extra_reports: && gff3-validate $options --format sarif -- '$name' > '$report_sarif' || accept_invalid #end if

param.name: run
param.label: Run the biology checks against a genome?
param.help: Compares features with the genome sequence: seqids and bounds, CDS phases, start, stop and internal stop codons, strand consistency (BIO-* rules).

param.name: genome
param.label: Genome FASTA
param.help: The genome the annotation was made on, plain or gzip/BGZF-compressed. Sequence names must match the GFF3 seqids.

param.name: translation_table
param.label: Translation table
param.help: NCBI genetic code used for start, stop and internal stop codons.
param.option: 4. The Mold, Protozoan, and Coelenterate Mitochondrial Code and the Mycoplasma/Spiroplasma Code
6. The Ciliate, Dasycladacean and Hexamita Nuclear Code
9. The Echinoderm and Flatworm Mitochondrial Code
11. The Bacterial, Archaeal and Plant Plastid Code
25. Candidate Division SR1 and Gracilibacteria Code

param.name: header
param.label: FAIR-bioHeaders (FHGFF3) header
param.help: How to treat a FAIR-bioHeaders provenance header (#~ lines).
param.option: Require it (a file without a header is invalid)

param.name: max_findings
param.label: Maximum number of findings to report
param.help: Counts of errors, warnings and notes stay complete.

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
`gff3-validator`_ checks a GFF3 annotation file against the `GFF3 specification 1.26`_ and explains every problem in plain language, with the rule id, the line and a suggested fix. It never changes the file.
Checks:
- **Syntax** (``GFF-SYN-*``): the ``##gff-version 3`` line, nine tab-separated columns, percent-encoding, seqid characters, coordinates, score, strand and phase. - **Attributes** (``GFF-ATT-*``): tag=value pairs, reserved tags such as ``ID``, ``Parent``, ``Target``, ``Gap`` and ``Dbxref``. - **Directives** (``GFF-DIR-*``): ``##sequence-region``, ``###``, ``##FASTA`` and others. - **Structure** (``GFF-STR-*``): unique IDs, resolvable ``Parent`` and ``Derives_from`` references, cycles, features within their sequence region. - **Biology** (``BIO-*``, only with a genome): seqids and bounds against the genome, CDS phases, CDS within exons, start, stop and internal stop codons under the chosen translation table, strand consistency. - **FAIR-bioHeaders header** (``HDR-*``): whether a FAIR-bioHeaders (FHGFF3) provenance header is present; it can be required or skipped.
Each finding has a level:
- **error**: the file is invalid; - **warning**: probably a mistake; the file stays valid; - **info**: a note; the file stays valid.
Every rule is described, with a bad example and a fix, in the `rule catalogue`_. The same validator also runs `in the browser`_, where files never leave the computer.
-----
**Input**
- A GFF3 file, plain or gzip/BGZF-compressed. - Optionally, the genome FASTA the annotation was made on (plain or gzip/BGZF), for the biology checks, and the NCBI translation table (default 1, the standard code; use 11 for bacteria, archaea and plastids).
**Output**
- An HTML report (always). - Optionally the same report as JSON and as SARIF 2.1.0 (both with the ``json`` datatype). - A text summary in the job's standard output.
**Job status**
A file with errors is a successful validation: the job finishes and the reports say the file is **INVALID**. The job fails only when validation could not be completed, for example when the input or the genome cannot be read or the genome cannot be indexed (duplicate sequence names, lines of different lengths inside a record); the reason is in the job's standard error.
**Limitations**
This is an early release (0.1.0) and the rule catalogue is a draft under review with the Sequence Ontology group:
- Sequence Ontology checks (that ``type`` is a valid SO term and that parent-child types agree) are not implemented yet; the report lists them under "not checked". - A few core rules are planned and not yet checked; the report lists them. - FAIR-bioHeaders header contents are not validated yet; only the presence of a header is checked. - Rule ids, levels and report formats may change before 1.0.
.. _gff3-validator: https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/gff3-validator .. _GFF3 specification 1.26: https://github.com/The-Sequence-Ontology/Specifications/blob/master/gff3.md .. _rule catalogue: https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/gff3-validator/blob/main/docs/rules.md .. _in the browser: https://fair-bioheaders.github.io/gff3-validator/
